text:
Maya: Heads up — after yesterday's kernel-selector tweak (fastpath preference), we've been seeing short-sequence tenants get starved when a few long requests show up. 30s+ tail for short seqs in a bunch of shards.

Jon: ugh. saw perfbot alerts?

PerfBot: [auto] 1758001300 - spike: P99 latency for <32-token requests increased from 42ms -> 520ms on g4d-prod-pool. KV hit rate unchanged.

Li: Quick hypothesis: selector now biases kernels that favor long-context throughput. That changes batching behavior (bigger per-batch token budgets) so short seqs wait for fill targets.

Tess: Also saw increased KV cache priming time. When long seqs hit and warm a KV stripe, they keep the batch open longer to amortize kernel setup; short seqs get queued behind.

Maya: attaching a tiny flame snippet:
```
# top of batcher timeline
batch_open at t=0 (long request)
kernel_switch cost=3.2ms
batch waits 12ms for more tokens -> accumulates long requests
short requests arrive @ t=2ms..8ms and wait until batch dispatch @ t=15ms+
```

Jon: So two levers: 1) kernel-routing bias (prefer short-path for small seqs) 2) queue/batcher policy (short-slot reservations / microburst slots / token budget caps).

Alejandra: Proposed quick experiment: keep current kernel selector but change admit policy to enforce a short-slot window (<=32 tokens) that dispatches after 2ms or after X items, whichever first. Shouldn't require kernel changes.

Li: +1 for short-slot. Also suggest a per-tenant micro-reservoir: each tenant gets small bucket of immediate dispatch credits to avoid head-of-line blocking. Credits refill slowly to avoid abuse.

Maya: we already have token credits but they refill in coarse epochs. Need smoothing. If we make refill continuous with leak-rate r, short bursts won't starve.

Tess: Concern: could increase kernel churn (more small kernels). But we can pair short-slot with kernel-hint: when admitting a short-slot batch, prefer fastpath kernels even if global selector favored another kernel. That hint-level override is cheap to implement.

PerfBot: Suggestion: run an A/B canary on 10% of shards with short-slot=2ms + per-tenant microcredits(8 tokens, leak 1 token/50ms). Monitor p99 and kernel-switch counts.

Maya: ok putting config sample here:
```
batcher.policy.short_slot.enabled = true
batcher.policy.short_slot.max_tokens = 32
batcher.policy.short_slot.max_delay_ms = 2
tenant.microcredit.initial = 8
tenant.microcredit.leak_ms = 50
kernel.hint.shortpath_override = true
```

Jon: telemetry we need: p50/p95/p99 by seq-length buckets (<32, 32-128, >128), kernel-switches/sec, batch_size distribution, KV-hit latency, tenant wait-time histogram.

Li: Also watch fairness metric: fraction of dispatches served by top-5% tenants over time window. If that climbs, microcredit is insufficient.

Tess: small caveat: when a long request arrives first and starts warming KV, short-slot may dispatch separately and reduce KV locality -> cost up. We should measure extra token compute and cost per token. If cost delta < P99 improvement, it's a win.

Alejandra: canary plan: 24h ramp on 10% shards (non-enterprise tenants), collect metrics above, rollback on any >2x cost delta or any regression for >5% tenants.

Maya: I've kicked off canary config rollout to shard set A (ids: a12,a13,a14). InfraBot will push the flag.

InfraBot: flag rollout started: /ops/flags/shortslot/canary -> shards a12,a13,a14. Monitoring streams: link https://grafana.company/r/shortslot-canary

PerfBot: baseline snapshots saved at ts=1758001280. Will compare to canary stamps.

Jon: If canary looks good, next iteration: tighten kernel selection logic to prefer low-latency kernels for short-slot by default (safer long-term). Also evaluate token-budget targets: reduce batch target for long-running kernels when there are queued short requests.

Maya: Agree. For now short-slot + microcredit + kernel hint is low-risk. I'll run through postmortem if canary fails.

Li: One more telemetry ask: add 'wait_reason' tags to requests (e.g., waiting-for-fill, waiting-for-kernel-switch, kv-warm) so we can attribute.

Alejandra: I'll add instrumentation patch this morning. ETA PR by EOD.

Tess: I'll prepare the cost/regression dashboard and slices.

Maya: Thanks all. Action items:
- Alejandra: PR short-slot metrics + microcredit instrument (EOD)
- InfraBot/Jon: monitor canary + set rollback alerts (now)
- Tess: cost dashboard (EOD)
- Li: prototype kernel-hint logic (next week)

Jon: :thumbsup:

Maya: :thumbsup: will report back in ~6h with initial canary numbers.
